architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.tie_interpretation: The deterministic VOI layer is indifferent among the tied top experiments: they share an identical component vector. Tie-breaking is therefore a genuine task left to the Agent, and any selection inside this set cannot have been read off the VOI ranking.
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: After verifying the reactive mass fraction as 0.8000 from material functionality, SI_15_60 must be below 3.80% in every one of at least two independent repeats. This supports formulation-level superlinear drift suppression relative to H-CORE's 7.61% linear-dilution prediction.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if the arithmetic mean SI_15_60 across at least two independent repeats is greater than or equal to 7.61%, the verified 0.8000 reactive-mass-fraction linear-dilution prediction. H-CORE is falsified if SI_15_60 is below 3.80% in every repeat. Values from 3.80% through below 7.61%, or mixed repeats crossing these thresholds, falsify neither hypothesis and require the specified follow-up.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run an acrylic-only 120 C matched-window hold using the same normalized reactive core, verified reactive mass accounting, preparation history, at least two independent repeats, and the same 15-60 min SI_15_60 observable; compare it with a matched dual-axis composition to test whether the minor tackifier-like axis is required.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = 100 * (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, reported as percent for each independent repeat
judge_normalized.rationale: The 120 C matched-window hold is the most direct and interpretable test of the unresolved viscosity-growth failure mode. S1C41 preserves both independently supported modifier axes while minimizing modifier burden among the genuine deterministic ties. A result below 3.80% would provide a formulation-level rheological outcome inconsistent with linear dilution alone, whereas a mean at or above 7.61% would reject the superlinear-suppression hypothesis. No molecular mechanism is inferred.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator in selecting S1C41::M-HOLD-120 because it directly measures the declared failure mode, lies in the supported two-axis region, and uses the smallest tied acrylic loading. I followed the Skeptic in narrowing the interpretation: the experiment tests bundled dual-axis suppression versus reactive-core dilution and cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL or attribute an individual modifier effect. I also resolved the Skeptic's operational objection by defining the repeat decision rules and requiring verified reactive mass fraction before applying thresholds.

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C melt residence, with modifier-dependent thermal-hold instability unresolved.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: At 120 C, the original E5 formulation increased by 51.54% from 15 to 60 minutes and 93.08% from 15 to 90 minutes, compared with 9.51% and 16.85% for E1 over the same windows.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only E1 and E5 have original isothermal-hold data, with four points over 15 to 90 minutes and no follow-up hold profiles. The temperature response has six measured points from 80 to 130 C across multiple runs and formulations, while the realized viscosity level has descriptive repeat-spread data for E2. Thus the time-dependent drift shape and its dependence on modifier axes are least resolved.
measurement_requirements: Measure viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes during a 120 C isothermal hold and report the matched-window SI_15_60 relative change.
Use at least two independent repeats with fully recorded preparation and hold histories so drift can be distinguished from realization variability.

Include a composition comparison that contrasts acrylic-like modification without minor tackifier-like modification against a composition with the minor tackifier-like axis active, while recording reactive mass fraction for the linear-dilution prediction.
Retain the full time trajectory rather than only an endpoint, and keep the temperature and time windows within the measured support.
planner.scientific_question: For a resin-modified composition measured in a matched 120 C hold, is viscosity drift substantially below the reactive-core linear-dilution prediction, and does reaching the low-drift regime require the minor tackifier-like axis rather than the acrylic-like axis alone? This separates H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If matched 15-60 min drift is below 3.80% across at least two repeats, the result supports H-RESIN over H-CORE because it is below half of the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction and exceeds the 2.00% resolution threshold. It also supports a low-drift dual-axis intervention, but cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL because both modifier axes are active.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If drift is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the result is consistent with H-CORE's linear-dilution prediction; H-DUAL is not independently adjudicated because the minor tackifier axis is present. A drift below 3.80% instead falsifies H-CORE and constitutes the low-drift acceptance outcome.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A drift between 3.80% and 7.61% does not meet the registered superlinear-suppression criterion and is not close enough to the linear prediction for an unambiguous mechanistic call; it would require additional matched-window experiments, especially an acrylic-only composition, to test H-DUAL.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: Deterministically tied, but its higher 17.5% acrylic loading adds modifier burden without increasing direct hypothesis-pair separation or measurement interpretability.
Deterministically tied, but its 20% acrylic loading is a larger perturbation than necessary for the same direct drift test and the same unresolved H-RESIN versus H-DUAL distinction.
Deterministically tied, but its 22.5% acrylic loading increases intervention magnitude without adding a separable registered hypothesis pair.
Deterministically tied, but its 25% acrylic loading is the largest supported perturbation and is not needed to obtain the direct matched-window discrimination.

proposer.reasoning: The failure mode is directly the 120 C isothermal drift coordinate, so M-HOLD-120 is preferable to model-fit sweep or anchor measurements. S1C41 lies inside the externally supported acrylic and minor-tackifier regions, uses the repeated approximately 5% tackifier cluster, and directly tests the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% against the registered superlinear threshold of 3.80%. It separates the reactive-core explanation from both resin-suppression and dual-axis interpretations, while explicitly leaving the resin-versus-dual distinction unresolved.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards are genuinely tied by the deterministic VOI components and directly measure the same supported 120 C drift coordinate. S1C41 uses the lowest acrylic loading in the supported 15-25% region and the repeatedly supported approximately 5% minor-tackifier region, giving the smallest sufficient modifier burden and smallest justified departure from the E2 reactive core while retaining the same two-axis hypothesis discrimination.

residual_decision_risk: Process-state variability remains uncontrolled by M-HOLD-120 and may confound threshold classification.
The phrase 'across at least two repeats' remains ambiguous unless the preregistered statistic specifies whether every repeat, the mean, or another rule determines classification.
H-RESIN versus H-DUAL remains unresolved because both modifier axes are active.
The 7.61% linear-dilution benchmark depends on verified material functionality and correct reactive-mass accounting.
The result can support a formulation-level rheological pattern but cannot establish the proposed molecular encounter-frequency mechanism.

The five-way deterministic tie is genuine; S1C41 is preferred scientifically for its lowest supported acrylic loading and smallest sufficient modifier burden, not because the VOI score ranks it above the other tied candidates.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is valid: S1C41 changes both modifier axes, so H-RESIN and H-DUAL make the same low-drift prediction and the experiment cannot establish that the minor tackifier axis is required or attribute effects to either axis separately. This does not change which experiment should be run for the stated immediate failure-mode test of resin-modified drift versus the H-CORE dilution benchmark. It requires restricting the interpretation to bundled dual-axis suppression and treating an acrylic-only matched-window hold, with a matched dual-axis comparison, as the necessary follow-up for H-RESIN versus H-DUAL. The repeat decision rule, preparation and hold-state recording, and verified reactive functionality must also be specified before applying the numerical thresholds.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposal remains top ranked in all 25 re-weightings. No recommendation_flip_boundary is reached for any weight term over the 0.5x-1.5x sweep, so no tested perturbation changes the tied top set. These weightings are defensible because the matched-window 120 C hold directly measures the declared failure mode, has high measurement interpretability, and discriminates the reactive-core dilution prediction from low-drift modifier behavior. The small base margin to the first strictly lower experiment is not operationally relevant within the reported sweep because top_experiment_set_stability and mean Jaccard stability are both 1.0.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The stated SI_15_60 thresholds are attainable from direct viscosity readings at 15 and 60 minutes, and the nominal H-CORE versus low-drift separation of 3.804 percentage points exceeds the declared 2.00% resolution. However, the protocol must specify whether "across at least two repeats" means every repeat or an aggregate and must control or quantify preparation and hold-state variability; otherwise the criterion is operationally ambiguous and vulnerable to the unaddressed process-state risk.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low SI_15_60 result could support resin-associated suppression but cannot establish that the minor tackifier axis is required or specialized; claims that the experiment separates H-DUAL from H-RESIN would be unsupported.
objections.objection: The selected S1C41 composition contains both AC1920 at 15.0% and TK100 at 5.0%, so H-RESIN and H-DUAL make the same low-drift prediction of 3.804%. The proposer correctly lists "H-RESIN vs H-DUAL" under hypotheses_not_separated, but the broader reasoning and the planner's scientific_question still describe the experiment as separating all three hypotheses. An acrylic-only matched-window hold is required for the registered H-DUAL test.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result would support only a bundled dual-axis intervention relative to the dilution benchmark, not a causal claim about either modifier axis or their distinct rheological roles.
objections.objection: The primary intervention changes both modifier axes simultaneously: AC1920 is 15.0% and TK100 is 5.0% in S1C41, while the reactive-core fractions are reduced to MDI 16.1525%, PDP70 31.9237%, and PPG2000 31.9237%. Consequently, any observed drift change cannot attribute an effect to acrylic modification versus tackifier modification, nor establish the claimed division in H-DUAL that acrylic relocates viscosity while tackifier suppresses drift. The proposal admits the H-RESIN versus H-DUAL entanglement but does not fully state that individual modifier-mechanism attribution is unavailable.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: If AC1920 or TK100 contains NCO-reactive functionality, the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction is miscomputed and the direct drift measurement would not support the stated comparison to H-CORE.
objections.objection: The primary observable SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 is directly computed from the protocol's 15 and 60 minute viscosity readings, with no model fit, extrapolation, or imputation. This attack surface largely survives. However, the use of the derived 7.61% benchmark depends on treating reactive mass fraction 0.8000 as correct for the selected materials.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A threshold outcome could be driven by preparation or hold-state variability rather than formulation behavior, making acceptance of H-RESIN or falsification of H-CORE non-reproducible.
objections.objection: The S1C41 criterion requires SI_15_60 below 3.80% or at/above 7.61% "across at least two repeats," but the protocol specifies only "at least two independent repeats" and does not define whether the criterion applies to every repeat, the mean, or a confidence bound. More importantly, M-HOLD-120 has process_state_risk 0.75 and explicitly does not control process state; six process fields are missing. Thus repeat-to-repeat realization variability can prevent a reproducible classification even though the nominal prediction separation is 3.804 percentage points and the declared resolution is 2.00%. The measurement can produce threshold-crossing numbers, but the protocol does not define a statistically valid decision rule for deciding that the threshold was met.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low drift value would be overinterpreted as proof of a molecular dilution or encounter-frequency mechanism that the planned viscosity trajectory does not measure.
objections.objection: The rheological hold measurement can test the formulation-level drift predictions, but it cannot establish the molecular mechanism stated in H-RESIN, namely reduced effective concentration and encounter frequency of reactive species in a non-reactive continuum. The registry's claim_boundary correctly says no molecularly resolved pathway is required, but the proposer should label the outcome as support for an operational formulation-level pattern rather than evidence for that molecular explanation.

skeptic.recommended_change: Add a preregistered acrylic-only 120 C hold with the same reactive-core normalization and at least the same repeat protocol, plus a matched dual-axis comparison. Define the decision statistic explicitly, require full preparation and hold histories, and recalculate reactive mass fraction from verified material functionality before applying the 7.61% benchmark.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The dual-axis composition confounds AC1920 and TK100 while the selected experiment is nevertheless described in parts of the proposal as separating H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL. Because H-RESIN and H-DUAL both predict 3.804% drift for S1C41, the experiment cannot determine whether tackifier is required or whether the acrylic axis has only a viscosity-level effect.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The phosphoric-acid-labelled E1 +P curve is not used in the chemistry-audited primary state model.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

voi_sent_to_model.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. voi_sent_to_model.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%.
